Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be caleld the claimant on this one, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in the front passenger seat of my friend's sedan. We were going through the intersection in Houston on a
green light, or at least that's how I remember it.
Q: Who was driving, and what direction were you traveling?
A: My friend was driving. We were heading east when a pickup coming from the north ran the red and hit us on the
driver's side, the side closest to me? No, actually the impact was on the passenger side where I was sitting.
Q: Let me clarify that. You said the pickup struck the passenger side. Was that the side where you were seated?
A: Yes, that's right. The door on my side took the hit and the whole car spun a little.
Q: Did you hit anything inside the vehicle or were you restrained?
A: I had my seatbelt on. My head snapped to the side and my shoulder slammed into the door frame.
Q: When did you first notice pain or discomfort?
A: Within a few minutes, my neck felt stiff. By the next morning my lower back was aching too, and turning my head to
check traffic hurts now.
Q: Have you souhgt medical care since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day and was told I had a neck and back strain. I've been doing
physical therapy twice a week sicne then.
Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this collision?
A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that stopped me from working
or exercising.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping and lifting groceries, and I'd like the claim to reflcet that.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
